title: Annotatio II §.III (3): Clement/Theodoret, Victor, Mark liturgy, Cyprian — Spirit’s virtue; spiritual presence only
pass_a_gloss: Finally (3) Theodoret, or rather Clement in the Epitome of the Stromata that are wanting, sets in the Sacred Supper an earthly substance as if impregnated with a singular divine virtue, i.e. the efficacy of the Holy Spirit, saying: Bread and oil are sanctified by the power of the names, not remaining the same according to appearance as they were taken into species, but by power are changed into spiritual power. Victor of Antioch declares these sayings of Clement more fully on Mark’s And as they were eating: God accommodating Himself to our infirmities sends into the proposed species the virtue of life and transmutes them into the efficacy of His own flesh, that we may have it unto vivifying participation. Exactly to the mind of the Greeks’ Liturgy called of St. Mark, in which God is asked to send His Holy Spirit upon the breads and cups, and sanctify and perfect them as almighty God and make the bread indeed body and the cup blood. St. Cyprian also reads its traces, saying the Holy Spirit is not only Author of the Thing owed to the Sacrament but also pours into the sacrament the fullness of His grace (On the Baptism of Christ). But all these, by these their utterances, introduce no other presence of Christ’s Body in the Sacred Supper than a spiritual one — both through the Author Spirit and through this Author’s operation and spiritual effect.
pass_b_english: (3) Clement (via Theodoret’s Stromata epitome): bread and oil change by the power of the names into spiritual power — not same in appearance.

Victor of Antioch, the Liturgy of St. Mark, and Cyprian speak of the Spirit sending life-virtue into the species — yet all introduce only a spiritual presence of Christ’s body, by the Spirit’s authorship and effect.
source_text: Denique (3) Substantiam terrestrem, singulari virtute divinâ, i. e. Spiritus Sancti efficacia, imprægnatam quasi, in S. Coena sistunt Theodoretus seu potiùs Clemens in Epitome Stromat. quæ desiderantur, dicens: Panem & oleum sanctificari τῇ δυνάμει τῶν ὀνομάτων, non eadem manentia κατὰ τὸ φαινόμενον, sicut in speciem assumpta sunt, sed δυνάμει εἰς δύναμιν πνευματικὴν μεταβάλλεσθαι — virtute in virtutem spiritualem mutari. Hæc Clementis dicta fusiùs declarat Victor Antiochenus ad illa Marci: Et cænantibus ipsis: Deus sese accommodans nostris infirmitatibus immittit propositis speciebus virtutem vitæ & ea transmutat in efficaciam ipsius carnis, ut in participationem vivificam eam habeamus. Prorsus ad mentem Liturgiæ Græcorum quam S. Marci vocant, utpote in qua rogatur Deus, ut immittat super panes & calices Spiritum Sanctum suum, & eos sanctificet & perficiat tanquam Deus omnipotens & faciat panem quidem corpus calicem autem sanguinem. Cujus quoque vestigia legit S. Cyprianus, Spiritum Sanctum non Autorem duntaxat Rei Sacramento debitæ esse, sed & sacramento plenitudinem gratiæ suæ infundere dicit, de Baptismo Christi. At, omnes hi, effatis his suis, Corporis Christi in S. Coena praesentiam, non aliam, quam spiritualem, tum per Autorem Spiritum, tum per Autoris hujus operationem, effectumque spiritualem, introducunt.
